newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM says Pol Pot may have left country.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM says Pol Pot may have left country.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh said on Thursday that Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot may have already left the country but Thai military sources familiar with the issue disputed this.
The premier's comments were in response to a report in a Thai newspaper on Thursday that Pol Pot and his top aides were in Bangkok en route to political exile in China.
In Bangkok, a senior Thai general who monitors Cambodian affairs and a Cambodian embassy official denied the newspaper report.

The spokesman for the Chinese embassy in Phnom Penh also denied the report. "The report on Pol Pot seeking exile in China is not true. We have no information of such a plan. They are all groundless reports," he added.

The Bangkok Post newspaper, citing Cambodian sources and field reports, said that the Moaist hardliner and his top aides, Son Sen and Ta Mok, had left Cambodia by crossing the border into Thailand on Sunday and were now in Bangkok.
"I cannot confirm or deny the report in the Bangkok Post, because I didn't read it. But he (Pol Pot) may have left already," Ranariddh told reporters.
When asked where Pol Pot may have gone, he said, "Don't ask that. I don't want to make problems with other countries."
Ranariddh said he wanted to bring Pol Pot to justice but felt that may now be impossible.

His comments contrasted sharply with those made by his co-premier Hun Sen on Wednesday that Pol Pot, Ta Mok and Son Sen were all still in the Khmer Rouge's northern Cambodian stronghold of Anlong Veng.

The Bangkok Post reported that Pol Pot's movement to China was part of an agreement reached with the Cambodian government to end a long-standing conflict between the government and the rebel Khmer Rouge.
Son Sen is the Khmer Rouge's defence minister while the one-legged Ta Mok is its army commander.

Ta Mok was known as the butcher of Cambodia during the Khmer Rouge reign of terror in Cambodia from April 1975 to December 1978. More than one million Cambodians died from executions, sickness, malnutrition and forced labour during the Khmer Rouge rule dubbed the "Killing Fields".
"I am very surprised at the report that Pol Pot is in Bangkok, it cannot be true," a Cambodian diplomat told Reuters.
He also dismissed the report that the Cambodian government had agreed a deal with the trio to leave Cambodia for exile in China.
"Pol Pot is the man most wanted by the Cambodian government for trial for his role in the genocide of Cambodian people," said the diplomat who declined to be named.
The Thai general, who also declined to be identified, said the report was untrue.

"It is impossible, the Thai government will never allow his passage via our soil," he said. "Pol Pot is a very sensitive and dangerous issue. No country wants to deal with him." A Thai businessman, who was Ta Mok's business partner in the past, said it was unlikely that Ta Mok would leave Cambodia because he had big businesses along the Cambodian border with Thailand.
Ta Mok, he said, had been investing in many businesses in the name of other Thai businessmen.

"Construction companies, petrol stations, and farm machine production facilities run by some Thai businessmen are widely known here as investment from Ta Mok," said the businessman based in Si Sa Khet province which borders the northern Cambodian town of Anlong Veng.
